title: Developer Experience Initiative: Portfolio prioritization & cycle commitment
creator: Maya Kim
description: Scope: Define a single prioritized portfolio of Developer Experience work (SDKs, docs, quickstarts, sample apps) we will commit to across the next two cycles, surface clear OKRs, and lock engineering/design capacity. This ticket captures the prioritization framework, selected initiatives, success metrics, rollout sequencing, and follow-up tasks for operationalizing measurement and maintenance. Outcome: a committed set of initiatives that map to 2 measurable OKRs, resource allocations per cycle, and a public roadmap for internal stakeholders.
updates: 2025-11-05 - Kickoff: alignment workshop with Eng, Design & Customer Success. Collected candidate backlog of ~34 items across SDKs/docs/quickstarts.
2025-11-19 - Prioritization rubric drafted (Impact x Confidence x Effort). PMs agreed on thresholds for 'commit' vs 'defer'. Draft stored: https://confluence.redwood.ai/devx/prioritization-rubric

2025-12-03 - Triage pass completed. Removed duplicates, consolidated 9 sample-app requests into a single 'starter-apps' initiative. Saved canonical list to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DevXPortfolio
2025-12-15 - Cross-functional review: Design requested a phased doc rewrite (tech notes -> quickstarts -> reference). Engineering flagged two high-risk infra deps (ENG-4782, ENG-5011).
2026-01-08 - Budget and capacity modelling: estimated 2 FTE design, 4 FTE eng per cycle for committed portfolio. Model: https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/DevXCapacityModel
2026-01-20 - Design review: quickstarts flow approved with new template. Follow-up: DES-219 to create template and example pages.
2026-02-10 - Engineering commitment: feature owners assigned, integration spikes scheduled. GitHub project created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/devx-portfolio/projects/4
2026-02-20 - Cycle commitment locked. Selected initiatives moved to planned in Cycle 2026-W09. Roadmap published internally: https://console.redwood.ai/roadmaps/devx-2026-Q1
comments: Diego Ramirez (2025-12-16): We should gate SDK surface churn with a compatibility test harness before broad rollout. Action: ENG-5011 to scope harness.
Aisha Patel (2026-01-11): Suggested success metric: reduce first-time SDK integration time from 45m -> 15m. Will own UX measurement.
Ben Chu (Engineering Lead, 2026-02-02): Recommend incremental rollout per language (Python -> Node -> Go). Adds 2-week stagger to schedule but reduces risk.
PRs to track: gh: redwood-inference/sdk-python#412, gh: redwood-inference/devx-docs#88
signals_and_metrics: OKR-1 (Adoption): 30% increase in trial projects using official SDKs within 6 weeks of release (baseline measured via console-project-tags).
OKR-2 (Time-to-first-success): Median time for a new developer to complete a quickstart from repo clone -> first API call decreases to <= 15 minutes.
Operational metrics: SDK install success rate, CI test pass rate (compat harness), quickstart drop-off points (docs analytics), number of support tickets referencing 'getting started'.
acceptance_criteria: Committed portfolio list published and approved by Eng + Design + Growth.
Resourcing model shows feasible allocation for two upcoming cycles with named owners.
Two OKRs defined with measurement dashboards wired and baseline collected.
Compatibility test harness scoped and ENG-5011 scheduled into next cycle.
Quickstart template delivered (DES-219) and at least one 'golden' quickstart implemented for Python.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Infrastructure dependency (ENG-4782) blocks multiple initiatives. Mitigation: parallel spike and fallback plan to use hosted mock endpoints.
Risk: Documentation overhaul takes longer than expected. Mitigation: phased approach with cutover milestones and smoke tests for each section.
Risk: Surface churn causes SDK breakage. Mitigation: compatibility harness and staged language rollouts.
Risk: Metrics noise from instrumentation gaps. Mitigation: early analytics spike to validate event schema before rollout.
